newsitem.title: CANADA: Aber A-154 South diamonds valued.
newsitem.headline: Aber A-154 South diamonds valued.

text.p: Aber Resources Ltd said diamonds from the A-154 South Pipe at the Diavik property in Canada's Northwest Territories were valued at an average US$56.10 a carat based on a sample of about 7,210 carats.
The valuation was done by CRA Diamonds, a unit of RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd which holds a 60 percent stake in the property through RTZ's Kennecott unit.
Aber said the A-154 South pipe had a final grade of 4.54 carats per tonne based on a sample of 2,585 tonnes yielding 11,739 carats.

Because of subjectivity in diamond valuation, Aber and Kennecott will have 2,500 carats from A-154 South pipe sorted and valued by independent diamantaires in Antwerp, Belgium. This independent valuation will be completed by year end.

Aber said a sample of 156.81 carats from 71.72 tonnes was recovered from the A-154 north pipe for an average grade of 2.19 carats per tonne. These diamonds were valued at US$35.30 per carat. "This was a small sample and not necessarily representative," Aber said.

The A-154 North pipe is located only 250 metres from the A-154 South pipe and in an open pit operation the upper one-third of the North pipe would be mined from the same open pit as A-154 South at minimal additional mining cost, Aber said.

Aber also hired a diamond consultant, Davy Lapa of Overseas Diamonds, N.V. based in Antwerp, to advise it on the sorting and valuation process and "to assist Aber in developing a marketing plan for its anticipated 40 percent share of diamond production."
Most analysts believe the Diavik property will yield a large-scale diamond mine and said the valuations for the A-154 South stones were very promising.
